title: Literary forms inside the knowledge units
statement: Teach poetry, drama and classic tales on texts inside the knowledge units, not in separate genre units, and check that every form the standards name appears.
detail: A Grade 3 reading course's BrainLift holds that genre and structure are best taught on the text being read, since a genre unit divorces form from content and uses up a slot that would otherwise build knowledge. An adversarial review of its draft found every literary unit was narrative prose, which left drama and poetry with no place, a hard fail against standards that name scenes and stanzas. The fix put a readers' theatre play, and a poem tied to each unit's knowledge, inside the knowledge units; the rule is the course's own position, with no measured outcome.

evidence.quote: poetry, drama, and classic tales belong inside the knowledge units, taught on the text at hand — not in genre units of their own.
A genre unit divorces form from content and burns the knowledge slot.
all literary units were narrative prose, leaving **drama and poetry orphaned — a hard CCSS fail**
